subject: Suggestions for a "getting started" guide for simple bifactor models?

messages.author: 3c5bb5f734cb1bc5
messages.subject: Suggestions for a "getting started" guide for simple bifactor models?
parts:
So, I'm interested in using mIRT in a very practical sense.  I've got a background in educational research and I'm fine with unidimensional IRT, but I mostly do 2pl models in STATA.  Totally unfamiliar with R, downloaded it and RStudio, got the mIRT package installed, and an hour of frustration and red errors later, threw up my hands and admitted my ignorance. I'm not a measurement expert nor am I going to publish in this area, and I'm mostly interpreting results for an audience with very little measurement experience.

What I want to be able to do is run bifactor models on live test data.  For example, I have a test from a biology professor with n=207 students, 30 items, and a belief that 7 of those items load on two constructs (critical thinking and biology knowledge) while the other 23 items just have the single factor (biology knowledge).  I'd like to be able to produce this sort of graph (found on the web) for those 7 items.  Ideally, theta-hats for both biology knowledge [from all 30 items] and critical thinking [from the 7 flagged items] would also be nice.

I think what I'm looking for is a "getting started" guide.  I found the wiki and was not having much luck replicating the code in there, but it is VERY possible that I'm doing things wrong.  Does anybody have a suggestion for a new person on where to start, if getting to this sort of model is the end goal?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Suggestions for a "getting started" guide for simple bifactor models?
parts:
There are several resources available to learn mirt, including workshop material, wiki logs, etc. I think your best bet is to start with the workshop material and read the documentation carefully, as well as execute the associated helpfile example code. You sound like you want to use the bfactor() function coupled with itemplot().

Phil
